question: Why did the error rate go up on 15 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v4.12 to ap-south caused the error rate to increase.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v4.12 to ap-south introduced a new version of the catalog.
The new version of the catalog was not fully tested and caused errors in the service search in region us-east.
The error rate increased from 0.48% to 1.12% after the deployment.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v2.24 to eu-west did not cause the error rate to increase.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v2.24 to eu-west was a routine release and did not affect the error rate in us-east.
The error rate increase was specific to the us-east region and the service search.
The error rate in other regions and services remained stable.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a sudden increase in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume and p95 latency did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a configuration change in the service search.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment of catalog v4.12 was the only change in the system.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search in region us-east rose from 0.48% to 1.12% (+131%), with a change point at 2026-03-15T04:10:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search in region us-east: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.11).
At the same time, request volume for service search in region us-east stayed about the same (1114 per 5 min before, 1250 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search in region us-east stayed about the same (141 ms before, 140 ms after, -1%).
Deployed catalog v4.12 to ap-south (catalog, ap-south; 4 min before the change; record R007)
Deployed catalog v2.24 to eu-west (routine release) (catalog, eu-west; 166 min before the change; record R006)

reasons: ✓ A change event (deploys) lines up in time (4 min before the change).
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records for the affected service/region
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of catalog v4.12 to ap-south.
Implement comprehensive testing for new catalog versions before deployment.
Monitor the error rate and request volume in the us-east region closely.
